Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

only adjective

the only one

also sole, only child, the only one

classical

Plaut. Trin. 4.4.21: hic ūnus, ut ego suspicor, servat fidem (Lewis & Short)
Ter. And. 1.5.46: ūnum hoc sciō (Lewis & Short)

ūnus, ūna, ūnum

adjective

only, alone (of all)

The plain word for “the only”: in quō ūnō acquiēscō, the only one I find rest in (Cic. Att. 9.10.1).

Examples

  • nūper diē quārtō, ut recordor, et certē aquārium urceum ūnicum domī frēgit

    the other day, four days ago as I remember, and I’m sure of it, he broke the only water jug in the houseGell. 10.24.10

  • circumsiliēns modo hūc modo illūc ad sōlam dominam ūsque pīpiābat

    hopping about, now here, now there, he kept chirping to his mistress aloneCatull. 3.9–10

Other words

  • ūnicus, ūnica, ūnicum — only, sole (one and no more)

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 41: fīlius ūnicus (Lewis & Short); Gell. 10.24.10: urceum ūnicum

    An only son or daughter is fīlius ūnicus, fīlia ūnica.

  • sōlus, sōla, sōlum — only, alone, sole

    adjective · also used · classical · Catull. 3.10: ad sōlam dominam; Plaut. Am. 1.1.269 (Lewis & Short)

    Genitive sōlīus, dative sōlī.

See also only, one.

SourcesLewis & Short: unus · Lewis & Short: unicus · Lewis & Short: solus
